title: Epoched golden dataset lifecycle + config-triggered eval orchestration
creator: Ava Kline
description: Define and deliver an 'epoched' golden dataset lifecycle and orchestration for automatically running curated evals when model or serving-config changes are detected. Goal is to reduce unnoticed regressions caused by infra/config drift and to give product and platform owners a clear audit trail for which golden snapshot was used for each regression alert.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Golden datasets can be created as immutable 'epochs' with signer, fingerprint, and human-readable changelog.
2) Config and model-change webhooks trigger a deterministic eval run against the latest eligible epoch.
3) Eval results are surfaced in Console with links to the epoch artifact, diff view vs previous epoch, and a regression severity score.
4) RBAC prevents accidental edits and requires steward approval to retire an epoch.
5) CI gating can block canary rollouts when regression severity > threshold and unblock after steward sign-off.
implementation_notes:
- Use content-addressed storage for epoch artifacts and SHA256 fingerprints.
- Store epoch metadata (tags, signer, changelog, retention policy) in the golden registry service (db schema version v3).
- Add webhook handlers to change-sentry that emit structured events for: model.version.change, runtime.config.patch, and quantization.profile.swap.
- Eval-orchestrator will schedule runs using an existing eval runner pool; runs should be idempotent and reference epoch fingerprint.
- Console: add an 'Epochs' tab in the Golden Dataset view; implement diff visualization (pass/fail per prompt + example failure traces).
- Backwards compat: if no epoch exists, fall back to legacy promptset behavior but mark evals as 'unanchored'.
risks:
- Storage costs for long-lived epochs.
- Spurious regressions due to non-deterministic evals; need to pair with variance-aware thresholds.
- Operational cost if evals are heavy; may need sampling.
- RBAC edge-cases: ensure signer key rotation doesn't orphan epochs.
rollback_plan: If initial rollout generates large false positives, revert to staged mode: disable automatic gating, surface notifications only, and require manual 'run and approve' flow for critical releases. All epochs remain readable and immutable so rollback doesn't lose artifacts.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprinting and metadata APIs.
- Integration tests: simulate model.version.change -> webhook -> eval run -> Console event.
- Canary: enable for internal 'sandbox' orgs first; validate alert noise is < 2/week.
- Post-deploy monitor: eval-run latency, cost per run, false positive rate vs baseline.
